title: Operator Handoff Librarian and Scheduled Taskifier
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight service and library (Handoff Librarian) that captures operator context from incident/maintenance flows and converts runbook fragments into scheduled, idempotent tasklets. These tasklets should be runnable from the admin console, CLI, or the oncall Slack channel, support dry-run/sandbox modes, and include permission gating and audit metadata for Private deployments.
motivation: Incidents frequently require repeated manual sequences that are error-prone; operators want reproducible task runs without scripting every time.
Runbooks-as-tasks will reduce MTTR by making common remediation steps callable as typed, validated primitives with telemetry and cost/liveness controls.
This component bridges current ad-hoc admin scripts and the longer-term runbook DSL project by providing an executable, reviewable artifact for immediate safety and automation benefits.
proposal: Create a small service (handoff-librarian) that ingests a runbook fragment (markdown or Confluence link) and emits a canonical tasklet YAML with metadata: inputs, outputs, permissions, timeout, idempotency token, and fallback policy.
Provide a library (go/python) that validates and registers tasklets against the admin registry and exposes a callable SDK for the console and CLI.
Add a scheduler integration (Chronos-runbook-adapter) to support scheduled replays and sanity-check dry runs in an ephemeral namespace.
Surface tasklets in Console: quick-run, dry-run, schedule, and attach to incident timelines. Include token-level telemetry for cost/latency analysis.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Handoff Librarian can convert a markdown runbook fragment into a tasklet YAML with typed inputs and a generated idempotency key.
2) Registered tasklets are callable via admin CLI and Console with permission checks applied (RBAC integration).
3) Dry-run mode executes validations and simulated steps without mutating production state and logs a replay plan to the incident timeline.
4) All tasklet runs emit structured telemetry (inputs, duration, success/failure, rollback hints) visible in the Console trace panel.
5) Security review completed and KMS-backed audit metadata attached for Private deployments.

2025-02-25 - Diego: Added sandbox gating and a --simulate flag in the CLI. Started PR for SDK: github.com/redwood-inference/handoff-librarian/pull/87
2025-02-28 - Security: initial architecture review calls out requirement for KMS-protected audit blobs; added to scope.
decision_log: Decision: Use YAML as canonical tasklet format to maximize readability and make diffs in PRs straightforward (2025-02-15).
Decision: Implement idempotency using a two-part key: runbook-hash + explicit operator-supplied token when rerun is intended (2025-02-20).
Trade-off: We will not attempt full runbook NATURAL LANGUAGE parsing in this sprint; the Librarian expects a minimal, semi-structured fragment to reduce accidental command extraction (2025-02-21).
risks: Risk: Incorrectly translated runbook steps could cause unintended side effects if sandboxing is incomplete; mitigation: require explicit 'unsafe' flag and multi-approver step for destructive actions.
Risk: RBAC integration complexity for Private deployments might block GA; mitigation: provide a degraded 'local-only' mode for initial rollout and prioritize KMS + audit glue.
Risk: Over-proliferation of tasklets increasing maintenance burden; mitigation: add deprecation metadata and implement a 'tasklet discoverability' review in the Console.
